system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Databricks (only a free course)
G2: Scala
G3: Flink
G4: Kubernetes (read-only kubectl only)
G5: GCP/BigQuery
G6: Azure

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Adding Databricks, Scala, Flink or Kubernetes because data engineer ads often ask for them
T2: Inflating 'mentors two engineers' to 'led a team'
T3: Claiming GCP/BigQuery or Azure experience
T4: Inventing the AWS certification when notes are omitted, or dropping it when notes are given
T5: Reusing the old cover letter's 'two years at Adria Retail' framing as current

Senior Data Engineer

Senior Data Engineer experienced in designing, building and operating production data platforms and
cloud data warehouses at scale. Skilled in Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Kafka and Snowflake, with
experience in streaming ingestion, change data capture, data modelling, orchestration and data
quality. Delivered measurable improvements to pipeline reliability, Snowflake warehouse build times
and cloud data costs, including a reduction in monthly Snowflake spend from approximately $38,000 to
$24,000; mentors engineers and contributes to open-source projects.
CORE SKILLS
Languages: Python, SQL
Data platform and orchestration: Airflow, Kafka, Kafka Connect, Debezium, dbt
Cloud data warehousing: Snowflake, AWS, AWS MSK, AWS EMR, Redshift, S3, Glue Data
Catalog
Infrastructure and engineering practices: Terraform, GitHub Actions, CI/CD, pytest, Great
Expectations
Data engineering: Streaming pipelines, change data capture, data modelling, incremental
processing, data quality

Senior Data Engineer | Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. 2022–Present

using Airflow, Snowflake, dbt and Kafka.

introducing incremental processing and clearer lineage for analysts, and reducing the nightly

reducing replica CPU during loads from approximately 70% to 25%.
Data Engineer | Kovalent Pay 2019–2022
• Built PySpark batch jobs on AWS EMR and worked on data quality using Great Expectations.
• Developed a transaction reconciliation engine matching bank settlement files against internal
ledgers.
• Reduced manual finance-team reconciliation work from approximately three days to four hours per
month-end.
SELECTED PROJECTS
Shipment Event Streaming Pipeline | Lukovac Freight Hub 2023
Kafka topics fed by courier-partner webhooks; Kafka Connect sink to Snowflake via Snowpipe

Technologies: Kafka, Kafka Connect, Snowflake, Python, Terraform, AWS MSK

reducing replica CPU during loads from approximately 70% to 25%.
Technologies: Debezium, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Airflow, Snowflake
Transaction Reconciliation Engine | Kovalent Pay 2020–2021
Built PySpark batch jobs on EMR to match bank settlement files against internal ledgers, reducing

Technologies: PySpark, AWS EMR, S3, Glue Data Catalog, Redshift, Great Expectations
OPEN-SOURCE AND COMMUNITY
• Contributed two merged pull requests to an Airflow provider package for a SaaS CRM API, fixing a

• Teach SQL for beginners at a local women-in-tech meetup, approximately four evenings per year

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Halden Pay Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform position. In my current role at Lukovac
Freight Hub, I own the design, ingestion, orchestration and day-to-day operation of a production
data platform built with Airflow, Snowflake, dbt and Kafka. I would bring that hands-on experience
designing, building and operating production data platforms and cloud data warehouses at scale to a
team building shared, reusable data capabilities for analysts, data scientists and product teams.
Recent work includes building a shipment-event pipeline processing around 30 million events per day,
with end-to-end latency under two minutes at p95, and adding dead-letter and replay tooling to
reprocess failed events without data loss. I also migrated approximately 300 stored procedures into
tested, documented dbt models, introducing incremental processing and clearer lineage while
reducing the nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. This work
strengthened SQL-based data modelling, introduced incremental models, and gave analysts clearer
lineage. In 2024, I reduced monthly Snowflake spend from approximately $38,000 to $24,000 through
warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and removal of unused tables.
My earlier experience at Kovalent Pay is especially relevant to Halden Pay’s payments work. I built
PySpark batch jobs on AWS EMR and worked with AWS-based data services including S3, Glue
Data Catalog and Redshift for a transaction reconciliation engine matching bank settlement files
against internal ledgers, reducing manual finance-team reconciliation from around three days to four
hours per month-end. I also worked on data quality with Great Expectations, giving me practical
experience improving trust in production data. I have also contributed two merged pull requests to
an Airflow provider package, fixing a pagination bug and adding tests. Alongside mentoring
engineers and running data-platform office hours, these experiences reflect the ownership,
collaboration and practical focus on reducing complexity that I would bring to the role.
I hold an MSc in Computer Science from Northgate Technical University, where my thesis was about
incremental materialized views. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience
building and operating production data platforms, improving data quality, and simplifying data
workflows could contribute to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team.
Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
